terms.gloss: exchange money, coin for coin or one currency for another
evidence: Plin. NH 33.45: placuitque dēnārium XVI assibus permūtārī
terms.comment: In business Latin, to exchange money, and to send it abroad by a bill of exchange (Cic. Att. 12.24.1; Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: an exchange of money; payment by a bill of exchange
evidence: Cic. Fam. 3.5.4: quae mihi ex pūblicā permūtātiōne dēbētur, (the money) due to me from the public exchange

phrases.latin: placuitque dēnārium XVI assibus permūtārī, quīnārium octōnīs, sēstertium quaternīs
phrases.english: and it was decided that a denarius should be exchanged for sixteen asses, a quinarius for eight and a sesterce for four

sources: Lewis & Short: permuto · Lewis & Short: permutatio
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. exchange (vb).
Pliny, NH 33.45, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (Mayhoff’s text), and Cicero, Fam. 3.5.4, against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 311.
